channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Zelenskyy says early warning system for Russian missile attacks resumes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the change happened after talks with his American counterparts, including a phone call with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

item.title: France announces nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris and other cities
item.description: Fresh curfews were being imposed across the city centers of Paris and Lyon on Tuesday after the first quiet night since France's most destructive rioting in years.

item.title: Firefighting planes and barbecue bans needed to combat Britain's wildfire risk, MPs warn
item.description: New firefighting planes and disposal barbecue bans are needed to tackle the growing danger of wildfires in the UK, MPs have urged.

item.title: US envoy Witkoff to meet Putin in Russia after 'positive' talks with Zelensky
item.description: US special envoy Steve Witkoff will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg Wednesday after talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. US news outlet Axios reported that Witkoff would be presenting Putin with an updated peace proposal on ending the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Tough new rules on Brazilian butt lifts and chemical peels proposed
item.description: Brazilian butt lifts and other cosmetic procedures that inject filler into parts of the body will only be performed by doctors under new government rules to crackdown on "cosmetic cowboys".

item.title: 'High percentage' of DOJ's noncitizen voters list was born in US: LA County analysis
item.description: The DOJ's list of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California includes a “high percentage” of people who say they were born in the U.S., L.A. officials said.

item.title: Jane Doe says she felt 'unsupported and disbelieved' by Cornell president
item.description: The former Cornell student who alleged she was gang raped at a fraternity house in 2024 said she felt "unsupported and disbelieved" by the school's president.

item.title: American Airlines flight blows tire while landing at Chicago O'Hare: FAA
item.description: The American Airlines Flight 41 crew "reported a brake issue and then a blown tire" after landing safely, the FAA said in a statement.

item.title: Boeing's 737 Max 10 finally wins FAA approval after years of delays
item.description: Boeing's largest 737 Max jet has cleared a major regulatory hurdle, with US aviation authorities approving the Max 10 for passenger service on Tuesday after nearly a decade of delays. The certification marks a boost for the planemaker's recovery, with deliveries expected to begin in 2027.

item.title: Live: French PM Lecornu to meet with unions ahead of new protests
item.description: After implementing curfews in cities across France to prevent a continuation of the weekend's violence and looting, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu prepared to meet with trade union organisations on Wednesday to discuss protest security and responses to the high school students who began the now nationwide protests. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Uganda reacts angrily as Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case
item.description: Nigeria has recorded its first case of Ebola during the current outbreak, the country's health ministry has said - as the virus continues to spread internationally.

item.title: Amy Acton campaign slams Ramaswamy over controversial ad featuring estranged mother
item.description: Ohio Gubernatorial Candidate Amy Acton’s campaign alleged her opponent's campaign is using her estranged mother in a controversial political ad against her.

item.title: WATCH: Great white shark leaps out of ocean off California's Marina Beach
item.description: A great white shark surprised visitors off Marina Beach, California, when it leapt out of the ocean as a beachgoer was taking a video.

item.title: Italy announces new security measures after Milan riots, deploying 500 soldiers
item.description: Italy announced tougher security measures on Tuesday after weekend riots in Milan left more than 100 police officers injured and shops looted. The government will deploy 500 additional soldiers, impose harsher penalties for violent protesters and hold parents financially responsible for damage caused by minors.

item.title: El-Sayed says Trump's attacks on his faith are to distract from pain he's causing
item.description: The Michigan Senate candidate said they don't address Americans' struggles.

item.title: Nigeria records first Ebola case as outbreak spreads across Africa
item.description: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in Africa's latest outbreak, while Kenya reported its ninth infection, raising fears of further spread across the continent. Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya warned of an “extremely serious threat” and urged the international community to send funding, medical supplies and health workers.

item.title: AI on the ballot? Voters in US midterms revolt against data centres
item.description: Two weeks out from the Midterm elections, there’s bipartisan pushback against data centers that suck the water and power out of communities. Just two years ago, ChatGPT was still a brand new thing, and AI was admired with awe by most voters. Like in 2024, the hot button issue in swing constituencies remains inflation or ‘the price of eggs’. But anxiety over the end of the month is now coupled with anxiety over the end of the world. In 2026, bots and large language models write papers and churn out campaign ads. We'll ask about calls for regulation despite fierce resistance from tech billionaires and whether the latest wobbles from the stock market signal that the race to corner the market and scale up at warp speed may be running out of road.

item.title: WATCH: Trump says what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine'
item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bill Taylor reacts to the latest comments from President Donald Trump on Russia as questions grow over America's support of Ukraine.

item.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case
item.description: In tonight's programme, Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case in the midst of an outbreak that began in DRC Congo in mid-May. Also, a former top South African police officer facing sexual grooming and rape charges is denied bail. Finally, São Tomé and Príncipe's rich volcanic soils produce vanilla pods with an entrancing taste unlike those grown anywhere else.

item.title: Egypt involvement in Yemen 'may actually weaken Cairo's regional role', expert says
item.description: Egypt's parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week, state media reported, after an emergency session ended without a decision a day earlier. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr May Darwich, Associate Professor in International Relations of the Middle East at the University of Birmingham. She explains that "this kind of military operation does not really have any objectives or exit strategy so at the moment this might actually weaken Egypt's regional role".

item.title: PSG end Barcelona's winning run as Liverpool fight back against Villarreal
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain came from behind to beat Barcelona 4-2 in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday, handing the Catalans their first defeat of the season. Liverpool staged a dramatic comeback to edge Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield, while Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens.

item.title: Lula's campaign seeks to disqualify Bolsonoro from Brazil presidential vote over Meta 'interference'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign is preparing to request the annulment of right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy over alleged social media interference from US tech giant Meta as Brazil’s presidential race intensifies ahead of Sunday’s runoff. The petition that will be submitted to the country's top electoral court claims "algorithmic manipulation" by Meta to suppress Lula's campaign content and boost Bolsonaro.

item.title: US regulators certify Boeing 737 Max 10 after years of delay
item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration has given final approval for the 737-10, the largest model in Boeing's best-selling Max family. The certification comes more than five years after the narrowbody jet's maiden flight, and marks an important step for the planemaker that's been trying to regain ground following a safety and management crisis. Plus, the French government has offered all businesses affected by the recent riots a interest-free loan of up to 50,000 euros.

item.title: ‘I’m alive’: Paris street medic isn’t dead, despite viral claims he was killed by police
item.description: A video showing French riot police violently beating a 26-year-old street medic in Paris has gone viral, with social media users falsely claiming he died from his injuries. But the street medic is alive, and spoke to FRANCE 24. The rumour was fuelled by confusion with a separate incident that same day: a man died of cardiac arrest in the same area, causing online users to conflate the two events. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: NJ food importer files lawsuit challenging Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods
item.description: A New Jersey food importer filed a lawsuit Tuesday challenging President Donald Trump’s power to invoke a Depression-era law to levy a 50% tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods

item.title: WATCH: DHS: Ukrainians Retain Protection Pending TPS Decision
item.description: While the temporary protected status for thousands of Ukrainians has expired, the DHS says they can remain for now. Ukrainian student Mariia Hlyten discusses her unclear future in the U.S.

item.title: Man charged after woman stabbed to death in Manchester
item.description: A 26-year-old man has been charged after a woman was stabbed to death in Manchester.

item.title: Trump campaigning in Republican strongholds amid slide in polls
item.description: With the midterm elections fast approaching, US President Donald Trump is stumping for candidates in states that he won by double digits in 2024. Despite what he says, it’s a sign of what Trump and the Republican party are fearing: with polls showing GOP support slip drastically even in some deep red states. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis has more.

item.title: Italy sends troops, toughens security laws after Milan clashes
item.description: Italy on Tuesday approved the deployment of 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy. A cabinet meeting on Tuesday also approved a series of security measures, including making the detention of minors easier and introducing the crime of "violent participation in a demonstration". FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome.

item.title: French PM vows 'massive' police deployment for new demonstrations
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Tuesday vowed a "massive" police presence at fresh protests called for the coming weekend, as he faced criticism over the handling of recent street violence. The eurozone's second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron. FRANCE 24's Ellen Gainsford reports.

item.title: 'Netanyahu is fighting for his political career', expert says a week ahead of crucial vote
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu basked in Donald Trump's endorsement on Monday ahead of close-fought elections, airing a phone call in which the US president predicted he would win and suggested they may again attack Iran together. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Simon Mabon, Professor of International Politics and Middle East Studies at Lancaster University.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Zelensky meets Witkoff as US-Ukraine relations sink to new lows
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was meeting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday in a ​bid to rescue relations that have sunk to new lows as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow and Kyiv has complained about Washington withholding vital defences. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kharkiv.

item.title: Hundreds put on immediate trial for ransacking city centres across France
item.description: Since the 17th of October over 2,000 people have been placed in police custody in France. Nearly 70% are adults. The trials which have gotten underway help shed light on their profiles, what they did, what's the proof and what penalty they're likely to face. FRANCE 24's Delano D'Souza reports.

item.title: New Paris curfew ordered in parts of city from 2100 GMT Tuesday
item.description: Paris police ordered a new curfew for parts of the city for Tuesday overnight, after one the previous night that authorities said resulted in calm being restored following weekend riots and looting. The fresh curfew runs from 2100 GMT Tuesday to 0400 GMT Wednesday and applies to the Republique public square in the city's central east, where many weekend clashes took place, and in the central les Halles district which is full of shops. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from central Paris.

item.title: Swimmer killed in shark attack in South Africa
item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed in a shark attack at a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast, local authorities said.

item.title: Trump attacks Democratic challenger Hamilton at Kansas rally as Senate race tightens
item.description: President Donald Trump took the stage in Kansas on Monday night to campaign for Sen. Roger Marshall, a one-term incumbent facing a close race against Adam Hamilton.

item.title: How French police are harnessing social media to identify looters
item.description: French police are turning to social media to identify and arrest suspects linked to last weekend’s looting and unrest. Investigators are scrutinising videos posted online alongside footage from thousands of security cameras to track suspects and gather evidence. The crackdown comes as the government vows to hold those responsible for the violence and damage to shops accountable.

item.title: Man arrested for alleged threats to shoot President Trump at Kansas rally
item.description: Authorities allege the man posted several threatening messages on Facebook.

item.title: Vanessa Kerry is the new WHO envoy for health resilience. What's on her to-do list?
item.description: A respected figure in the world of global health, Dr. Kerry takes on a new responsibility. She says it's challenging but not "daunting."

item.title: More than 150 killed in Sudan drone strike on disputed Abyei border region
item.description: At least 153 people have been killed in a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region, where a fire at a nearby fuel depot continued to burn on Tuesday. Local officials blamed Sudan’s military for Monday’s attack, which also left dozens injured.

item.title: France: Local curfews imposed after protests
item.description: French cities that imposed a curfew Monday saw a generally calm night, after October 17 protests devolved into violent riots this past weekend. Despite criticism from citizens, France's government said it is maintaining the measure where necessary on Tuesday night.

item.title: France's decades-long ties with Gulf states built on 'economic development, oil, defence agreements'
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome François Gouyette, former French ambassador to the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Against a backdrop of violent unrest at home and escalating conflict in the Middle East, French President Emmanuel Macron's Gulf diplomacy underscores the increasingly blurred boundaries between domestic economic security and international strategic commitments. Ambassador Gouyette argues that the visit serves a dual purpose: alleviating France's energy pressures while reaffirming its longstanding defense partnerships with Gulf monarchies. Insisting that "France has to play its role as a key partner," Gouyette portrays French military assistance as an expression of strategic solidarity rather than direct participation in the war with Iran.

item.title: Two men re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran after RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Two men have been re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service over a suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford.

item.title: Some older siblings left raising family members after parents' deportation: Advocates
item.description: Some older siblings have been left to care for their younger family members following the deportation of their parents, advocacy groups say.

item.title: WATCH: Wirecutter shares top picks after 15 years of product testing
item.description: Jason Chen of The New York Times' Wirecutter shares the technological products that are most loved by readers.

item.title: Some changes are coming for Medicare as open enrollment begins
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare, the nationwide federal health insurance program primarily for those aged 65 and older, began last week and there are some changes.

item.title: WATCH: Funding cuts forcing World Food Program to reduce lifesaving aid in Gaza
item.description: ABC News' Ian Pannell reports on the state of the agency, which says it's been providing food to around 1.6 million people every month since last year's ceasefire announcement.

item.title: Suspect arrested in France after fire at historic city hall
item.description: A man has been arrested after a fire at the town hall of Limoges, according to French media.

item.title: Neglect in hospital contributed to baby's meningitis death, jury rules
item.description: Neglect contributed to the death of a five-month-old girl who died from meningitis after opportunities were missed in hospital to save or prolong her life, an inquest jury has found.

item.title: Four soldiers from UN-backed force missing after gang attack in Haiti
item.description: Four soldiers from El Salvador are unaccounted for after being attacked by heavily-armed gangs in Haiti.

item.title: About 6 in 10 Americans confident election will be conducted fairly, accurately: Poll
item.description: Most Americans are not confident Trump will accept midterm results if GOP loses.

item.title: What if an AI bubble bursts — and that accelerates AI job losses?
item.description: Research on past recessions suggests downturns can accelerate automation. That raises the specter of a double whammy for workers.

item.title: WATCH: Study shows Gulf oil spill's lasting damage
item.description: More than 16 years after the BP oil spill off the Gulf Coast, new research reveals lasting damage to marine life.

item.title: Albanians set fire to government buildings and clash with riot police in latest protests
item.description: Demonstrators in Albania have set fire to government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows during the latest clashes with police as they demand the prime minister's resignation.

item.title: WATCH: Trump announces fuel relief for farmers
item.description: President Donald Trump took his midterm pitch to Kansas Monday night, announcing a new fuel relief program for farmers facing record-high diesel prices.

item.title: Oil-rich Alberta votes to remain part of Canada in historic referendum
item.description: Alberta ‌has voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation.

item.title: Trump's approval rating hits new record low as US midterms loom
item.description: Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low - indicating that next month's midterm elections could be punishing for the Republicans.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir reports on the beloved barn owls that have made Manhattan home
item.description: An expert says it’s the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history.

item.title: WATCH: Teen on how he turned 3D printing idea into a profitable business
item.description: Just three months after graduating high school, Mike Satterlee began using his 3D printer to make hard-shell insulated drink koozies he calls "can coolers."

item.title: Report set to reveal vast scale of antisemitism in English schools
item.description: A landmark report is set to detail the vast scale of antisemitism in English schools and colleges, Sky News can reveal.

item.title: Japan launches mission to Mars to bring back samples from its moon
item.description: Japan launched a spacecraft towards Mars in a ground-breaking mission to bring back samples from the largest of the planet's two moons.

item.title: WATCH: Is using cash for purchases becoming a thing of the past?
item.description: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill are considering bills to keep cash an option in commerce.

item.title: UEFA writes to FIFA demanding answers on Trump-Infantino dealings
item.description: European football chiefs have sent a list of 42 questions to FIFA, demanding answers about Gianni Infantino's alleged "conflicts of interest" over business dealings with the Trump family and the World Cup sell-off attempt.

item.title: Doomsday cult leader found guilty of murdering 190 children and one adult
item.description: Doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie, his wife Rhoda Maweu, and 29 other co-accused have been found guilty of the murder of 190 children and one adult.

item.title: WATCH: Blind student, guide dog enjoy adventures in Scotland
item.description: ABC News' Danny New interviews a blind college student in Virginia who's traveling with her guide dog Beasley as she continues her education in Scotland.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.
